question: Is the seed-89 Band A attractor cluster_457 a locally isolated point, or a sample from a soft (L-direction) family — i.e. does the LC residual grow fast in every local direction?
hypothesis: Distinguishing strict (cluster_457 genuinely off truth's polhode) vs charitable (the 1.1% Casimir mismatch is just polish residual the LC can't see) via controlled local perturbation; the strict reading holds if both L-direction and polhode-scaling sweeps are stiff.
narrative_md: Perturbed cluster_457 in two families (L-direction rotation at fixed body polhode; polhode/Casimir scaling at fixed L direction) and rendered 63 hi-fi LCs vs seed-89 truth. Every direction is stiff — exits Band A-union-B at +-2 deg of inertial rotation and +-0.5% scaling, including the twist-about-L control. Conclusion: cluster_457 is a locally isolated point, closing the charitable polish-residual reading; the strict 'different polhode' reading holds. N=1; does not bear on cohort-wide cat-4. Renders vs truth LC and perturbs truth-derived state -> oracle_clean false.
